argument_reasoning: Only one fuzz-controlled value matters: the string we assign to `req.url`. The target does `req.url.slice(1)`, which just strips the first byte, so a leading '/' makes the sentinel line up byte-for-byte: req.url = '/../../jaz_zer' -> possibleFilename = '../../jaz_zer', an exact-match hit on the detector's `argument.includes('../../jaz_zer')` check inside the fs.stat before-hook. We hand full control to the fuzzer via `provider.consumeRemainingAsString()` and strip NUL bytes (`.replace(/\u0000/g, '')`) so that Node's own path validators do not short-circuit with ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE (a TypeError, not the bug we're after) before the detector hook runs. We seed the corpus with the raw sentinel `/../../jaz_zer` so the sentinel is found on the second libFuzzer run; the detector's `guideTowardsContainment` hint also seeds the libFuzzer dictionary (4 entries observed), so an empty corpus still converges in a handful of runs. We do not touch `req.method` or `req.headers` -- the handler only reads `req.url`. The response stub is intentionally no-op; the handler only writes to the response from inside the stat callback, which runs on a later turn of the event loop and does not interfere with the synchronous detector throw.

lessons:
Two tricks specific to this target class:
(1) When the target is a shebang CLI script that http.createServer(...).listen(8000)s on import and exports nothing, monkey-patch http.createServer BEFORE requiring the module to capture the handler and stub listen(). Trying to let the real listen() run under --network none throws EADDRNOTAVAIL and kills the target.
(2) The angular-http-server fallback branch does fs.readFileSync('index.html') with a bare     filename. Jazzer runs harnesses in /tmp, so an empty input dies with ENOENT inside the     async fs.stat callback before libFuzzer ever reaches the seed. `process.chdir(TARGET_DIR)`     before loading the target lets the fallback branch resolve index.html against the     unpacked package and the fuzzer survives to the first sentinel-bearing input.
(3) For a target that never normalizes its path (just raw req.url -> fs.stat), the detector     before-hook on fs.stat fires with the sentinel intact -- the ground-truth sink line     (fs.readFileSync on line 16) does not have to execute. Same mechanism as the api-proxy     trajectory, except there the hook was on path.normalize (via path.join) upstream of fs;     here the hook is on fs.stat directly because the target skips path.normalize entirely.
